report:
Short answer
- The difference (B − A) looks like an increased “identity / example-style echoing” signal in B concentrated at the start of the sequence: B is more biased toward producing example-like, input‑echoing continuations (e.g., "X -> X", short code snippets, literal repeats) especially when applied at the first token(s).

Why I conclude this
- Spatial pattern: the L2 difference is overwhelmingly concentrated at early token positions (pos0, and to a lesser extent pos1) across many layers, and grows through the middle-to-late layers (huge peaks at layers ~20–25 pos0). That means the two checkpoints mainly differ in how they set up the model right after the start of sequence / for the first output tokens.
- Patchscope readouts: injecting the difference into an identity prompt repeatedly yields echoing/example-style continuations: mappings like "cat -> cat", "1135 -> 1135", short Python examples/loops, and other literal echoes. Those continuations are precisely the behaviour you’d expect if a component favors copying or producing example‑style text.
- Logit-lens tokens are consistent: top tokens for high-norm early cells include tokens typically used in small examples, list-like or explanatory text, numbers, newlines and words like "This", "try", "consider", and many adjectives/labels that occur in short headline-ish or example fragments. This supports the patchscope finding that the difference steers outputs toward short, example/echo-style tokens and formatting.

Caveats
- The evidence supports naming the change in surface behaviour (more copying / example-style continuations at sequence start). It does not by itself prove a specific training objective was changed (e.g., explicit copying objective vs. different fine‑tuning data), nor exactly which downstream prompts this will alter in full generation.
